Risk Management/Trading: Reading Material

These two terms are really synonymous...trading = managing risk.

I can't even think of what "non-risk management trading" would be

Trading is protecting the P&L. 

Giving back $1M on a winner and losing $1M on a loser are the same P&L of $1M, and represent the same poor management of risk, or failure to take profits, et cetera.

Books/Specific Interviews

This is strange but the best interviews on risk management that I've ever read, are consistently from commodity traders or ex-commodity traders.

And I say that from an equity analyst perspective. They are the most disciplined loss cutters.

From Market Wizards: the Kovner and Seykota interviews and others (Eckhardt), plus anything with PTJ of course.

I'm not huge on blogs/videos/podcast so I'm sure there's tons of "3 hour PTJ interviews," but the Return on Time is atrocious on all these.

You're looking for actionable insight you can use in your process, there might be 5 minutes in there. These two were pretty dense with good information: 

https://t.co/NHDUpHmk30

https://t.co/I7MhVKLE1L

Series/Titles: Market Wizards, John Train's books, Inside the House of Money

Basically, anything by Schwager, Train, or Drobny should fit the bill...they consistently do good work. They are the "core" of this genre.

Beyond that?

There is really not that much. 

I was just pinging LLM's and the titles they are suggesting are straight trash.

Part of this post is simply: do not waste time on these secondary/tertiary "trading" recommendations (Howard Marks? Taleb?) or historical non-fiction "risk management" about some bank that blew up.

None of this will help you become a better trader or risk manager, it would be like reading Liar's Poker it has a trading desk in it.

Once you read some of those OG market wizard guys, like Kovner, you will see what actual trading/risk management commentary looks like.

A lot of the memoirs I've read, I wouldn't demand that you use your time on them. Poor Return on Time, minimal actionable insight.

The Lefevre book on Jesse Livermore is a classic and should probably be on here, but the highlights will be in an LLM....you'll get 99% of the info and save 99% of the time.

Psychologists: May as well add everything by Mark Douglas and Ari Kiev here, it's trading-adjacent but it's psychology.

--

That's the end of the list. 

Feel free to reply or DM titles but I just vetted all the LLMs pretty heavily, and none of it is worth your time on a relative/opportunity cost basis.

Meaning, I'm benchmarking these books to, you spending time on something like Mauboussin or Buffett, or the other titles in my pinned tweet.

Beyond that, I have loose thoughts in these articles which are most useful in laying out, here are the various schools of thought available to you.

good luck trading,
GB
